title: The Last Confluence
logline: Threads meet in a membrane that shares without giving the house away.
epigraph: Unity that forgets its tributaries becomes empire, not river.
description: Chapter 12 of Lore.Land: The Last Confluence. All narrative threads meet. Merger without amnesia. Many hands on one turn; a visible seam; sources remain addressable. The egg rides the current.

content.text: Two rivers met under a low bridge. Boof stood at the edge of the clearing, the last bloom still on her whiskers. Before them a new

children.text: opened — not a maze, not a game. A membrane of current where the waters shared a turn without erasing their sources. Gold rope marked the splice. The egg rode the seam. Many hands could take one turn here, or none of them would.

content.text: The path was quiet and full of provenance. Boof knew the journey had changed. This was about walking forward with every tributary still named. A quote in the current still belonged to its shelf. You could walk upstream from any merge.
"You’ve come far, Boof," the Fool’s voice was almost kind. "The path ahead is yours. Share through the membrane. Do not give the house away."

img.alt: Two rivers meeting under a low bridge, a visible gold seam of current, the cracked egg riding the confluence.

content.text: Boof looked down the joined water and felt a calm that had nothing to do with neatness. Sources remained addressable after merge. The egg, a cell still keeping its own law, did not dissolve into the river. It rode. Downstream the archive had left a door open — shell-shaped, inspectable, a whole history a small reader could check.

content.text: "Where does it lead?" Boof asked. The Fool didn’t answer, and she felt no frustration. It mattered that the tributaries were still walkable. She followed the seam toward the last door.

loreItems.description: Confluence is a publishing problem: how to ship a whole without flattening provenance.
A membrane shares a turn without giving the house away. Sources remain addressable after merge.
Many hands on one turn: the operation happens entirely, or not at all.
